name: Consolidated Edison
description: Con Edison is a holding company for regulated delivery utilities: Consolidated Edison Company of New York (CECONY) sends electricity to about 3.7 million customers in New York City and Westchester, gas to about 1.1 million, and steam to about 1,490 customers in Manhattan; Orange and Rockland (O&R) serves about 0.3 million electric customers in southeastern New York and northern New Jersey plus gas customers. It owns almost no generation; it buys power and gas and passes the cost through, earning money on delivery and on a return (9.40% allowed ROE in the CECONY plan from 2026) on its rate base, set in multi-year New York rate plans. It sold its Clean Energy Businesses (solar and wind developer) on March 1, 2023 for a gain, leaving a pure utility with a small transmission investment arm.

businessLines.name: CECONY electric
businessLines.how: Customers pay a delivery charge each month set by multi-year New York PSC rate plans, plus the pass-through cost of electricity bought from the NYISO market; revenue-decoupling means delivery revenue is reconciled to the authorised level whatever the volume sold.
businessLines.description: Electric delivery and full-service supply in New York City (except part of Queens) and most of Westchester County to about 3.7 million customers.

businessLines.name: CECONY gas
businessLines.how: Regulated delivery charge plus pass-through of purchased gas cost, under the same multi-year plan with revenue decoupling.
businessLines.description: Gas delivery to about 1.1 million customers in Manhattan, the Bronx, parts of Queens and most of Westchester.

businessLines.name: CECONY steam
businessLines.how: Customers pay regulated steam rates for heating and cooling steam, with fuel and purchased-steam costs recovered.
businessLines.description: Steam distribution system, described as the largest in the United States, delivering about 16,975 MMlb a year to about 1,490 customers in parts of Manhattan.
